title: Splitter, aggregator and enricher
summary: Break a message into parts, put results back together, and add data from another system.

steps.title: Splitter
body: A **splitter** turns one message with many items into many messages with one item each.
An order with three lines becomes three messages, one per book, so each can be checked against the
warehouse independently.
```yaml
- split:
expression: { jsonpath: { expression: "$.lines[*]" } }
steps:
- to: { uri: "direct:checkStock" }
Each part remembers where it came from: Camel sets `CamelSplitIndex` (0, 1, 2), `CamelSplitSize` (3) and
`CamelSplitComplete` (true on the last part). Copy the parent's correlation id (here the order id) onto each part.

steps.title: Aggregator
body: An **aggregator** does the reverse: it collects related messages and combines them into one. It needs three decisions:
1. **Correlation**: which messages belong together? (the order id)
2. **Completion**: when is a group done? After `n` messages (`completionSize`), after a quiet period
(`completionTimeout`), or when a predicate says so.
3. **Strategy**: how to merge two messages into one (append to a list, sum, keep the latest).
Camel's `split` can aggregate its own parts directly with an `aggregationStrategy`, which is the
**scatter-gather** shape: fan out, then gather the answers.

steps.prompt: An aggregator completes on `completionSize = 3`. One of the three stock checks for order A1 is lost. What happens?
options: Group A1 waits forever (and holds memory) unless you also set a completion timeout
The aggregator completes with two parts after one minute by default
The other two messages are redelivered
steps.explain: Always pair a size with a timeout, and decide what a partial result means for the business ("2 of 3 lines confirmed").

steps.title: Enricher and content filter
body: - A **content enricher** calls another system to **add** data: take each order line and add the current stock
level from the warehouse. In Camel: `enrich` (calls an endpoint and merges the answer) or `pollEnrich`
(reads from a file or queue).
- A **content filter** **removes** data: drop `internalCost` before the message leaves. (Not to be confused
with the *message filter*, which drops whole messages.)
Both are just transformations with a purpose. Name them so a reviewer knows the intent.

items: Combine three stock answers into one order summary
Add the warehouse's stock level to each line
Wait until all parcels of a shipment are scanned, then send one event
Look up the customer's name from the CRM by id

steps.title: Split an order
prompt: Write `List<Exchange> Split(Exchange order)`. The body is an order:
Return one exchange per line, in order:
- `Body` = that line as compact JSON, `{"isbn":"9780131103627","qty":2}`. Build it with `JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { isbn, qty })` rather than `GetRawText()`, which keeps the sender's spacing;

- a copy of every header of the order, plus `OrderId` (the body's `orderId`, e.g. `"A1"`), `SplitIndex` (the same 0-based index) and `SplitSize` (the number of lines), all as strings. Don't add them to the original order's headers.
An order with no `lines` (or an empty array) returns an empty list.
solution: if (!root.TryGetProperty("lines", out var lines) || lines.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Array) return result;
Body = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { isbn = line.GetProperty("isbn").GetString(), qty = line.GetProperty("qty").GetInt32() }),
foreach (var (k, v) in order.Headers) part.Headers[k] = v;
hints: `foreach (var line in lines.EnumerateArray())` with a counter.
Copy the order's headers into each new part's dictionary, then add the three new ones.
template: Dojo.Eq("part ids", new List<string> { "ex-9-0", "ex-9-1" }, dojoParts.Select(p => p.Id).ToList());
Dojo.Check("parts don't share the order's headers", !dojoOrder.Headers.ContainsKey("SplitIndex"), "you wrote into the original order's headers");
Dojo.Eq("no lines -> no parts", 0, Split(new Exchange { Id = "e", Body = "{\"orderId\":\"B\"}" }).Count);
Dojo.Eq("empty lines -> no parts", 0, Split(new Exchange { Id = "e", Body = "{\"orderId\":\"B\",\"lines\":[]}" }).Count);
public Dictionary<string, string> Headers { get; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
public Dictionary<string, object?> Variables { get; } = new();

steps.title: Aggregate the answers
prompt: Each split part was checked against the warehouse. The answers come back **in any order, interleaved across orders**.
`string? Offer(string orderId, int expected, string isbn, bool inStock)`:
- return `null` until `expected` answers for that order have arrived;
- on the completing answer return `"{orderId}: {n}/{expected} in stock"`, followed, if any are missing, by `" missing "` and the out-of-stock ISBNs sorted and joined with `,`:
- then **forget** the group, so memory does not grow (a later answer for the same id starts a new group).
- `int OpenGroups` returns how many groups are waiting.
starter: public string? Offer(string orderId, int expected, string isbn, bool inStock)
solution: readonly Dictionary<string, List<(string Isbn, bool InStock)>> groups = new();
public string? Offer(string orderId, int expected, string isbn, bool inStock)
if (!groups.TryGetValue(orderId, out var list)) groups[orderId] = list = new();
var missing = list.Where(x => !x.InStock).Select(x => x.Isbn).OrderBy(x => x, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToList();
return missing.Count == 0 ? text : text + " missing " + string.Join(",", missing);
hints: A `Dictionary<string, List<(string Isbn, bool InStock)>>` keyed by order id.
When the list reaches `expected`, remove the key before returning the summary.
template: Dojo.Eq("A1 first answer -> waiting", null, dojoAgg.Offer("A1", 3, "978-1", true));
Dojo.Eq("B7 first answer -> waiting", null, dojoAgg.Offer("B7", 1 + 1, "978-9", true));
Dojo.Eq("A1 second answer -> waiting", null, dojoAgg.Offer("A1", 3, "978-3", false));
Dojo.Eq("B7 completes, all in stock", "B7: 2/2 in stock", dojoAgg.Offer("B7", 2, "978-8", true));
Dojo.Eq("A1 completes with missing isbns sorted", "A1: 1/3 in stock missing 978-2,978-3", dojoAgg.Offer("A1", 3, "978-2", false));
Dojo.Eq("a single-line order completes at once", "C1: 0/1 in stock missing 978-5", dojoAgg.Offer("C1", 1, "978-5", false));
